not_comparable_to: the headline test kappa 0.7001, which is measured on a 15-subject subset of BOTH cohorts - a different population

decomposition.finding: The 0.187 kappa drop is concentrated in Wake, and is a PRECISION failure rather than a detection failure. Wake recall on ST is 72%, in line with every other stage; wake precision is 55%. SC is 29.8% wake and ST is 9.9%, a 3x prior shift - the largest of any stage - so the SC-trained model over-calls wake by 1.32x. Physiology compounds it: SC is a ~20h cassette recording whose wake is largely daytime, ST is a lab night whose wake is brief arousals.
decomposition.how_to_report: Report kappa WITH this decomposition. Kappa alone reads as 'does not transfer'; the decomposition shows sleep-stage discrimination largely survives and one stage's base rate moved.
decomposition.SUPERSEDED_30_AUG: The 'driven by a 3x prior shift' attribution below is WITHDRAWN. Oracle prior correction recovers only 1.2% of the gap (prior_adaptation.json). The decomposition's FACTS stand - wake precision 55%, recall uniform at 67-72%, priors shifted 3x - but the causal claim does not. The gap is covariate shift.
